one_liner: Apify has a broad REST API (v2, OpenAPI published) with self-serve API-token auth, OAuth 2.0 for integrations, and an official hosted MCP server at mcp.apify.com.
auth_notes: Users generate an API token in Console and send it as a Bearer header (recommended) or token query param. The hosted MCP server supports OAuth sign-in, and the integration guide says Apify supports OAuth 2.0. The pages don't show how a third party gets OAuth client credentials for the REST API, so API token stays primary.
access_notes: Any user can create an API token in Console. The fetched pages describe Apify as freemium but give no explicit free-plan or credit details, so the free-tier terms are unverified.
blocker_notes: Usage is billed against platform credits. The exact free allowance isn't confirmed by the fetched pages.

evidence.quote: **You can create an API token on the [Integrations](https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations) page in the Apify Console.**
*(Recommended)* Add the token to your request's `Authorization` header as `Bearer <token>`.
The recommended remote connection signs you in with OAuth instead.
The API is organized around [RESTful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer) HTTP endpoints.
You can download the complete OpenAPI schema of Apify API in the [YAML](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.yaml) or [JSON](http://docs.apify.com/api/openapi.json) formats.

The Apify's MCP server ([mcp.apify.com](https://mcp.apify.com)) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) (MCP).
